seo.title: Sound Design | Igor Szuniewicz
seo.description: Sound redesigns: God of War combat, Baldur's Gate spells, weapon synthesis, sci-fi ambience. Original recordings, no library shortcuts.

hero.title: Sound Design Work
hero.subtitle: Redesigns where I replaced all original audio with my own recordings and processing. No library shortcuts.

video1.title: God of War — Combat Redesign
video1.description: I muted the original audio and rebuilt everything. The axe hits are metal-on-meat recordings I layered in Reaper. Shield blocks have that sharp crack because I compressed the transient hard and let the tail ring out. The enemy screams took the longest to get right.

video2.title: Baldur's Gate 3 — Spell FX Remake
video2.description: Fire spells start with a gas-burner recording pitched down an octave, then I added synth crackle on top for the magical layer. Ice is mostly granular synthesis with a slow attack so it sounds like it's forming. Each element needed to feel physically different when you hear it cast.

video3.title: Weapon Sound Design
video3.description: Same exercise, opposite directions. The P2000 pistol is foley and field recordings: mechanical clicks, a dry close-mic shot, room reflections added back in post. The sci-fi weapon is pure synthesis and spectral processing. Sounds like electricity arcing through glass.

video4.title: Fractured Horizon
video4.description: My first sound design project ever. Replaced all audio for a sci-fi scene: spaceship hum, alarm tones, mechanical doors sliding open. Honestly basic stuff, but this is where I learned how much timing matters. A door sound 3 frames late looks completely wrong.
